mainTopic: Two topics: (1) the source that a sacrifice slaughtered by a מתעסק (someone acting without awareness) is פסול; (2) whether the owner's intention, and not only the כהן's, can make an offering פיגול.
overview: The גמרא first looks for the source that a קרבן slaughtered by a מתעסק, someone not paying attention to the act, is פסול. ״ושחט את בן הבקר״ shows that this is the proper way to do the מצוה, and ״לרצנכם תזבחהו״ shows that it is required. Next, the גמרא notes that our משנה's rule, that only the person doing the עבודה can ruin the offering with his thoughts, disagrees with רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי. He holds that the owners can also cause פיגול, and רבא gives his source, ״והקריב המקריב״. אביי then says that three תנאים hold that when one person thinks and another acts, the thought counts: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי with קרבנות, רבי אליעזר with slaughtering for a non-Jew, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר with carrying on שבת. The גמרא shows that these views are linked in one direction only. Whoever applies the idea in a weaker area must accept it in a stronger one, but not the other way around. Then פרק בית שמאי ends, and the new פרק, איזהו מקומן, begins with a משנה about where each קרבן is slaughtered. קדשי קדשים are slaughtered in the north. The משנה describes the blood service of the יום הכיפורים bull and goat, and then of the bulls and goats that are burned, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where do we learn that slaughtering without awareness disqualifies?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a קרבן slaughtered by a מתעסק is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that someone who handles sacred offerings without paying attention makes the offering invalid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question: what is the source that a מתעסק, someone who slaughters without meaning to slaughter, makes the קרבן פסול?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מתעסק is not thinking about the act at all. For example, he means to cut something else and happens to slaughter the animal. The question assumes this ruins a קרבן and asks which פסוק teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who does an act without intending to do that act

phrases.english: From where do we know, regarding one who acts unawares with sacred offerings,
that it is invalid?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a מתעסק disqualifies a קרבן.

steps.title: First source: the slaughter must be for the sake of the bull
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from ״ושחט את בן הבקר״: the slaughter must be done with awareness that it is slaughter of the bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it says, "And he shall slaughter the young bull before ה׳". This means the slaughter must be done for the sake of the young bull.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer brings a פסוק showing that the שחיטה must be done consciously, as the slaughter of this animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "he shall slaughter the young bull" are read to mean that the slaughter has to be aimed at the bull. A מתעסק has no such awareness, so he does not fulfill the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of, with intent toward

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְשָׁחַט אֶת בֶּן הַבָּקָר לִפְנֵי ה׳״
phrases.english: As it says: "And he shall slaughter the young bull before ה׳"
meaning: not unless the slaughter is
for the sake of a young bull.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְשָׁחַט אֶת בֶּן הַבָּקָר לִפְנֵי ה׳״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק ״ושחט את בן הבקר״ requires the slaughter to be done for the sake of the bull.

steps.title: That only proves a מצוה, not that it is required
steps.stepSummary: The questioner objects: we already know it is a מצוה, but where do we see that the קרבן is invalid without it?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This we already have. But from where do we know that it is indispensable?
steps.whatsHappening: The other speaker pushes back. The פסוק shows the right way to do it, but it does not show that the קרבן is ruined if it was not done that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In קדשים, a פסוק telling you how to do something often only teaches the ideal way (לכתחילה). To say the offering is פסול after the fact, you need proof that the requirement is לעכב. The first פסוק does not give that.

keyTerms.meaning: This we already have in hand (we already know this)
To be indispensable, so that failing it invalidates

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the first answer is being thrown out. It stands as the source for the מצוה. The challenge only asks for a further source to show that the קרבן is invalid without it.

phrases.english: He said to him: This we already have in hand;
phrases.notes: Meaning: we already know it is the proper way to do the מצוה.

phrases.english: from where do we know it is indispensable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the source in step 2 proves invalidation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from ״ושחט את בן הבקר״.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק only establishes the proper way to do the מצוה, not that its absence disqualifies the קרבן.

steps.title: Second source: slaughter it with your awareness
steps.stepSummary: ״לרצנכם תזבחהו״ is read as ״לדעתכם זביחו״: the slaughter must be done knowingly, and this is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: "With your will you shall slaughter it" means: slaughter it with your awareness.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer brings a new פסוק that makes awareness a requirement, so the slaughter of a מתעסק is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רצון, "will," is read as דעת, "awareness". The פסוק conditions the slaughter itself on being done knowingly. That provides the indispensable requirement the challenge asked for.
steps.whatToRemember: A מתעסק makes a קרבן פסול. ״ושחט את בן הבקר״ teaches the מצוה, and ״לרצנכם תזבחהו״ teaches that it is required.

phrases.english: He said to him: "With your will you shall slaughter it"
meaning: slaughter with your awareness.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: We had only a source for the מצוה, not for invalidation.

steps.title: The משנה: only the one doing the service matters, and a תנא disagrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that intention follows only the person performing the עבודה, and notes that this is not like a certain תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "Because the intention follows only the one doing the service." Our משנה is not in line with this other תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and announces that a certain תנא holds differently. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to our משנה, only the כהן who does the עבודה can ruin the קרבן with improper thoughts. The owner's thoughts do not count. The גמרא is about to show an opinion that disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in accordance with this תנא

phrases.english: "Because the intention does not follow
anyone except the one performing the service."
Our משנה is not in accordance with this תנא

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per the משנה, only the performer's intention can disqualify; this is noted as a disputed position.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי: the owners can cause פיגול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, who heard that the owners can make an offering פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי said, "I heard that the owners can make the offering פיגול."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that shows which תנא disagrees with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owners' improper thoughts can make the offering פיגול, then the intention does not follow only the person doing the עבודה. That directly contradicts the משנה's rule.

phrases.aramaic: – דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: As it is taught: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי said:
I heard that the owners can render it פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the תנא referred to in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That some תנא disagrees with the משנה's rule.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבא asks for רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the reasoning of רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the reason of רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks for the source behind the opinion that the owners can cause פיגול. He answers it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner does not perform the עבודה himself. So we need a reason why his thoughts should count at all.

phrases.english: רבא said: What is the reason
of רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for owners causing פיגול.

steps.title: The source: ״והקריב המקריב״
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls the owner ״המקריב״, the one who offers, so his intention counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says: "And he who sacrifices shall sacrifice."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question with a פסוק that treats the owner as the one bringing the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner is called ״המקריב״ even though the כהן does the work. Since he counts as an offerer, his improper intention can also make the קרבן פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who offers (here, the owner)

phrases.english: For the verse says: "And he who sacrifices shall sacrifice."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״והקריב המקריב״ treats the owner as an offerer, so his intention counts.

steps.title: אביי: three תנאים hold that one person's thought counts when another acts
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר all hold that if one person thinks and another acts, the thought takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר all hold that when one person has the thought and another does the act, it counts as an intention.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי states a general principle and lists three תנאים who share it. The גמרא will now show where each one holds it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This makes the idea bigger than owners and פיגול. The principle is that a thought can be effective even when it belongs to someone other than the person doing the act.

keyTerms.meaning: One person thinks and another performs

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns one unusual opinion into a shared principle, and that principle sets the agenda for the steps that follow.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: אביי said: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: and רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
all hold:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה מְחַשֵּׁב וְזֶה עוֹבֵד – הָוְיָא מַחְשָׁבָה.
phrases.english: when this one has intention and that one performs, it is an intention.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר כּוּלְּהוּ סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three תנאים hold that one person's intention is effective even when another performs the act.

steps.title: The first of the three: what we just said
steps.stepSummary: For רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, the source is the ruling just quoted, that owners can cause פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי: this is what we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins backing up אביי's list. For the first name, it points back to the ruling that the owners can cause פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner thinks and the כהן acts, yet the owner's thought counts. That is exactly the case of זה מחשב וזה עובד.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן.
phrases.english: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי: that which we said.
phrases.notes: It points back to his ruling that the owners can make the offering פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי – הָא דַּאֲמַרַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins showing where each תנא listed in step 9 holds the principle.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי holds זה מחשב וזה עובד הויא מחשבה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His ruling that owners can cause פיגול (step 6).

steps.title: Source for רבי אליעזר: slaughtering for a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר disqualifies an animal a Jew slaughters for a non-Jew. This shows that the non-Jew's thought affects the Jew's act.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where does רבי אליעזר say this? As we learned in a משנה: If someone slaughters an animal for a non-Jew, the slaughter is valid. But רבי אליעזר says it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving the source for the second name on אביי's list, רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jew does the slaughtering, but the non-Jew is the one with the intention. Since רבי אליעזר says the slaughter is invalid, the non-Jew's thought must count for the Jew's action. That is exactly the idea of 'one thinks, another acts.'

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters on behalf of a non-Jew

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer: as we learned in a mishna:
One who slaughters for a gentile,
his slaughter is valid,
but Rabbi Eliezer deems it unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources for אביי's statement, moving from רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי to רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds one person's thought counts for another's action.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in חולין: רבי אליעזר disqualifies slaughter done for a non-Jew.

steps.title: Source for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: storing and carrying on שבת
steps.stepSummary: If one person stores something people don't usually store, and another person carries it out on שבת, the carrier is liable because of the first person's thought.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where does רבי שמעון בן אלעזר say this? As we learned: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר stated a rule. Take anything that is not normally worth storing, and that people do not store. If one person found it worth storing and stored it, and someone else came and carried it out, the carrier is liable because of the thought of the one who stored it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the third name on אביי's list, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, a person is normally liable for carrying only items that are considered worth keeping. Here, the item became worth keeping only because the first person stored it. Even so, the second person who carried it is liable, so one person's thought counts for another person's action.

keyTerms.meaning: To store away, to put aside for keeping
He carried it out (from one domain to another on שַׁבָּת)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar: as we learned,

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar stated a principle:
Anything that is not fit to be stored,
and people do not store things like it;
if it was deemed fit by this one and he stored it,
and another came and carried it out,
this one is liable through the thought of that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the last of the three sources for אביי's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds one person's thought counts for another's action.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His rule about storing an item and someone else carrying it out on שבת.

steps.title: These two surely agree with רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר apply this idea even outside the מקדש. So they would surely apply it to קרבנות inside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them hold like רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי. If we say this rule even for things outside the מקדש, do we even need to say it for things inside?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now compares the three views. It says that the two תנאים we just saw must agree with רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר. Ordinary slaughter and שבת are cases where thought matters less, and these two still let one person's thought count for another's act. So with קרבנות, where thought matters a lot (פיגול), they would certainly agree that the owner's thought counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it even necessary to say?

phrases.english: Both of them accept
phrases.notes: Both of them means רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: the view of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei;
now, if outside we say it,
phrases.notes: Outside means outside the מקדש: ordinary slaughter and carrying on שבת.

phrases.english: is it necessary to say it inside?!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְוַיְיהוּ אִית לְהוּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing all three sources, the גמרא checks how the views depend on each other, starting with the stronger direction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר would certainly agree with רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי about קרבנות, by קל וחומר.

steps.title: But רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי may not agree with them
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי might apply the idea only to קרבנות inside the מקדש, and not to ordinary matters outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי does not necessarily hold like the two of them. Maybe we say this rule only inside the מקדש, but outside we do not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the link works in one direction only. רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי might limit his view to קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי has a special reason for קרבנות: the פסוק calls the owner ״המקריב״ (step 8). That reason does not apply to ordinary slaughter or שבת. So agreeing about קרבנות does not mean he agrees about matters outside the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not hold, do not accept

steps.whatToRemember: The two views are linked in one direction only. Whoever says 'one thinks, another acts' outside the מקדש must agree inside it. But someone who says it for קרבנות (רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, based on ״המקריב״) may not agree outside.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as saying all three hold exactly the same thing in every case. The גמרא is narrowing אביי's list: רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי's view might cover only קרבנות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei
does not necessarily accept the view of both of them;
perhaps it is inside that we say it,
but outside we do not say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לֵית לְהוּ דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse direction of step 13 and shows that it does not follow.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The other two must agree with רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, but he does not have to agree with them. His rule may be limited to קרבנות inside the מקדש.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר would surely agree with רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון בן אלעזר applies one person's thought to another's act even on שבת, he would surely apply it to עבודה זרה, which is רבי אליעזר's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר agrees with רבי אליעזר. If he says it even about שבת, does he need to be told it about עבודה זרה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now compares the two rabbis from steps 11 and 12. It says that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר would surely accept רבי אליעזר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says one person's thought counts even for שבת, which has nothing to do with the מקדש. עבודה זרה is closer to Temple service, so his idea applies there all the more. This uses the same 'if here, then surely there' reasoning as step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (used to open a 'surely' argument: if even here, then all the more there)
Is it even a question? (meaning: obviously)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר –
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds like Rabbi Eliezer:
now, if regarding Shabbat we say it,
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 12: one person stores the item, and the other carries it out.

phrases.english: is it even a question regarding idol worship?!
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר's case from step 11: a Jew slaughters an animal for a non-Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After separating רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי from the other two, the גמרא now compares those two rabbis with each other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever applies one person's thought to another's act for שבת would surely apply it to עבודה זרה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר might not agree about שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר may apply the idea only to עבודה זרה, which resembles Temple service. For שבת, the Torah forbids only work done with the doer's own intent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר does not necessarily agree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Maybe you say this about עבודה זרה only because it is like service inside the מקדש. But for שבת, the Torah forbids only מלאכת מחשבת, planned work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the other direction. It shows that agreeing in one direction does not mean agreeing in both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה is similar to the service inside the מקדש, where another person's thought can matter. שבת is different: you are liable only for מלאכת מחשבת, work done with your own planned intent. The carrier in step 12 did not have that intent, so רבי אליעזר could rule he is not liable.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold / does not accept (that view)
Similar to the service inside (the מקדש)
Planned, intended work: the only kind of work the Torah forbids on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: The two rabbis agree in one direction only. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר (who covers even שבת) surely covers עבודה זרה. But רבי אליעזר (עבודה זרה) may not cover שבת, because שבת requires מלאכת מחשבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that 'one person's thought affects another's act' works differently in different areas of הלכה. It depends on how close the area is to Temple service and on its own rules, like מלאכת מחשבת for שבת.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר –
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer does not necessarily hold like Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar:

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הוּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ כְּעֵין בִּפְנִים,
phrases.english: perhaps it is regarding idol worship that you say it, since it is similar to the service inside,
phrases.notes: 'Inside' means inside the מקדש, where sacrifices are brought.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שַׁבָּת – מְלֶאכֶת מַחְשֶׁבֶת אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: but regarding Shabbat, the Torah forbade only planned work.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the opposite direction from step 15. It shows that the 'surely' reasoning does not work in reverse.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר may limit the idea to עבודה זרה, since it resembles Temple service. שבת requires מלאכת מחשבת from the doer himself.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק is finished. This line is the traditional goodbye to the chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not part of the discussion. It marks the end of the chapter and expresses the hope to learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
The name of this פרק, taken from its opening words

phrases.english: We will return to you, Beit Shammai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.

steps.title: New פרק: where קדשי קדשים are slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה asks where each type of קרבן is offered. It begins with the rule that קדשי קדשים are slaughtered in the north of the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: What is the place of the קרבנות? קדשי קדשים are slaughtered in the north.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins. Its משנה lays out the locations for the different קרבנות, starting with the holiest ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening question sets the topic of the whole משנה: where things are done with each קרבן. The first general rule is that קדשי קדשים, the most holy קרבנות, must be slaughtered on the north side of the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Where is their place? (also the name of this new פרק)
North (the northern part of the courtyard)

steps.confusionAlert: This is a brand-new topic. It has no connection to the discussion about one person's thought and another's act that just ended.

phrases.english: Mishnah: What is the location of the offerings?
Offerings of the most holy order: their slaughter is in the north.
phrases.notes: This means the north side of the courtyard in the מקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשי קדשים must be slaughtered in the north of the courtyard.

steps.title: The יום הכיפורים bull and goat: slaughter in the north and three inner blood placements
steps.stepSummary: The פר and שעיר of יום הכיפורים are slaughtered in the north, and their blood is collected there. Their blood is sprinkled between the בדים, on the פרוכת, and on the מזבח הזהב. Each one of these placements is essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bull and the goat of יום הכיפורים are slaughtered in the north, and their blood is caught in a holy vessel in the north. Their blood must be sprinkled between the poles of the ארון, on the Curtain, and on the golden altar. If even one of these placements is missing, the service does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first example of קדשי קדשים: the bull and goat of יום הכיפורים, and how their blood service is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This applies the opening rule from step 18, that קדשי קדשים are slaughtered in the north, to a specific case. It then lists three blood placements, all inside the מקדש: in the קודש הקדשים and in the היכל. The משנה stresses that all three are required, so leaving out any one invalidates the whole service.

keyTerms.meaning: The special bull and goat sin-offerings brought on יום הכיפורים
A holy vessel used for the Temple service
Between the poles of the ארון, inside the קודש הקדשים
The Curtain between the היכל and the קודש הקדשים
Holds back. The offering is invalid without it.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the 'golden altar' (מזבח הזהב, the inner altar in the היכל) with the outer altar in the courtyard. All three placements here are inside the building.

phrases.english: The bull and the goat of Yom Kippur —
their slaughter is in the north,
and the collection of their blood in a service vessel is in the north;
and their blood requires sprinkling
between the poles,
phrases.notes: These are the carrying poles of the ארון, so this sprinkling happens inside the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: and on the Curtain,
and on the golden altar —
each one of these placements is indispensable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first specific type of קדשי קדשים under the general rule from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יום הכיפורים bull and goat are slaughtered and their blood is collected in the north. Their blood needs three inner placements, and each one is essential.

steps.title: Leftover blood is poured on the western base, but this is not essential
steps.stepSummary: The שירי הדם of the יום הכיפורים offerings are poured on the western יסוד of the outer altar. If this was not done, the offering is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן would pour the leftover blood on the western base of the outer altar. If he did not pour it there, the offering is still valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the יום הכיפורים case by explaining what happens to the leftover blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the משנה draws a contrast with step 19. The three inner placements are essential, but pouring the שירים on the יסוד is a מצוה that does not hold back the offering. So the service is complete once the inner placements are done.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood left over after the required placements
The western base of the altar
The outer altar in the courtyard
It did not hold it back. The offering is still valid.

steps.whatToRemember: For the יום הכיפורים offerings, the inner sprinklings are essential, but pouring out the leftover blood is not.

phrases.english: The leftover blood he would pour
on the western base
of the outer altar,
and if he did not put it there, it does not invalidate the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the יום הכיפורים case, setting the non-essential leftover blood against the essential inner placements.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leftover blood is poured on the western יסוד of the outer altar, and leaving this out does not invalidate the offering.

steps.title: Bulls and goats that are burned: north slaughter and blood on the Curtain and golden altar
steps.stepSummary: For פרים הנשרפים ושעירים הנשרפים, slaughter and collection of the blood are done in the north. Their blood is sprinkled on the פרוכת and on the מזבח הזהב. The משנה's sentence continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bulls and goats that are burned are slaughtered in the north, and their blood is caught in a holy vessel in the north. Their blood must be sprinkled on the Curtain and on the golden altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves on to the next group of קדשי קדשים: the bulls and goats that are burned. It begins describing their blood service, and the rule continues in the following line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These offerings follow the same pattern as the יום הכיפורים ones: slaughter and collection happen in the north. The difference is that there is no sprinkling between the בדים. Only two inner placements are listed: the פרוכת and the מזבח הזהב.

keyTerms.meaning: Bulls whose bodies are burned outside the camp, not eaten
Goats whose bodies are burned outside the camp, not eaten

phrases.english: Bulls that are burned and goats that are burned —
their slaughter is in the north,
and the collection of their blood in a service vessel is in the north;
and their blood requires sprinkling
on the Curtain and on the golden altar —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next type of קדשי קדשים, following the pattern of the יום הכיפורים offerings but without the sprinkling between the בדים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bulls and goats that are burned are slaughtered and their blood is collected in the north. Their blood is sprinkled on the פרוכת and the מזבח הזהב.
